changes.rationale: July 22 issuer release describes Google investment in the LCOS subsidiary as a strategic partnership to expand production for applications including Google Glass. Parent retains majority control; partnership capital fits class 6. Closing conditions are distinct from announcement.

May 14 joint release announces BMS/Celldex combination-immunotherapy clinical collaboration, $5 million payment and shared development costs. This is a collaboration announcement rather than trial results.

March 27 Form 8-K states the issuer announced that South Africa's Supreme Court of Appeal upheld the SASSA tender process and award to its CPS subsidiary. Favorable contract litigation resolution fits class 9; later legal developments are outside this event review.

August 29 issuer release reports Remodulin patent enforcement and an injunction against Sandoz generic marketing through October 2017. Mixed ruling preserved: the separate patent expiring in 2029 was not infringed.

January 7 release confirms two previously unresolved customer contracts, with about $6 million expected Q1 revenue impact and future Gainshare fees. Filing archive lists January 7 at 4:08 p.m., consistent with the January 8 reaction. Acceptance timing is not proof of earliest public release; existing jump attribution retained.
August 6 issuer release reports Q2 results and increases annual guidance. Existing August 7 reaction attribution remains earnings-led; guidance within results does not qualify separately as class 8.
October 22 issuer release reports Q3 financial and operational results and schedules an October 23 morning call. Existing next-session earnings attribution retained.
November 12 issuer release reports Q3 financial results, the first quarter completed as a public company. Existing November 13 reaction attribution remains class 1.

May 18 issuer release reports Q1 financial results including first quarterly profit and rapid revenue growth. Existing May 19 earnings-reaction attribution retained; operational and product commentary inside results does not change the primary category.
November 11 issuer release reports Q3 results and raised annual guidance. Recent contract and product announcements are concurrent context; existing earnings-led attribution retained.

April 11 release announces IFC subscription for 9.98 million new shares, about an 18% stake, at a premium. Primary transaction is equity financing with expansion proceeds and board nomination rights; no defined operating collaboration or license is announced. Do not infer class 6 from supportive investor commentary alone.

Issuer-distributed MIIT sedan approval release is dated June 5, five calendar days before this June 10 jump. Category could be class 7, but the located source does not establish a fresh same-session catalyst. Defer for timing/continuation review rather than auto-promote.

Issuer 8-K says Anacor announced the $100 million arbitration award October 17, while counterparty Valeant release is dated October 18. Legal-unlock category is supported, but exact October 17 announcement time is unresolved. Defer reaction-session assignment; preserve historical Anacor issuer-identity warning.

Cisco physical-access partnership fits class 6 in substance. Syndicated issuer text is dated April 15; April 16 market coverage attributes the jump to the agreement. Exact initial announcement time is not recovered, so defer timing instead of assuming an after-close release.

Contemporaneous August 30 market account attributes the move to Jefferies upgrading the shares; pivotal myeloma results were still expected. No new trial result or regulatory approval is established by this source. Retain analyst-only exclusion.
